items.title: Doug Carn interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, February 24, 2023
items.q: You know Rodgers, Hammerstein get all of that money you know, as if they wrote it.

ctx.x: Those 52 choruses of “Crescendo and Diminuendo” that Paul Gonzalves played, he don’t get no money for that, you know what I mean? And all the great solos with all that stuff, Trane played on “My Favorite Things,” You know Rodgers, Hammerstein get all of that money you know, as if they wrote it. You know? And but see where it came from was way back in the day before “Bye-Bye Blackbird” and them other songs, and “Tiger Rag” and stuff. You know you’d play the record and then the little stuff you did in between like…
in, and especially bebop, they started adding more music to the composition than the composition had in the first place. You know what I’m saying?
